questions.question: How much computation can KG-FiD save with its early reranking setting, and which model is its main baseline?
questions.reference_answer: About 60% of the computation cost (with L1 = L/4 and N2 = N1/5); the main baseline is FiD.

evidence.quote: we can reduce about 60% of computation cost
We mainly compare KG-FiD with the baseline model FiD

questions.question: Which generator does the unified-knowledge-interface approach use for data-to-text, and on which test set is it evaluated intrinsically?
questions.reference_answer: It fine-tunes the pretrained T5-Large model as the generator; the intrinsic evaluation uses the DART test set.

evidence.quote: we use the pretrained T5-Large (Raffel et al., 2020) model as our generator
intrinsic evaluation on the DART test set

questions.question: What size of model does KGT5 use in its main experiments, and which two large knowledge graphs does it use to test link prediction?
questions.reference_answer: A model with the architecture of T5-small (about 60M parameters) trained without the pretrained weights; link prediction is tested on Wikidata5M and WikiKG90Mv2.

evidence.quote: a model with the same architecture as T5-small
We evaluate the link prediction capability of KGT5 on Wikidata5M

questions.question: How does ConditionalQA score an answer that comes with conditions, and what makes its questions hard?
questions.reference_answer: The score of the predicted answer is multiplied by the F1 of the predicted conditions against the oracle conditions; answering requires compositional logical reasoning across complex context.

evidence.quote: the scoring function will also take into account the accuracy of predicted conditions
Answering the questions requires compositional logical reasoning across complex context

questions.question: What is the maximum length of the paths SQUIRE samples for training, and what kind of model does it use to turn a query into a path?
questions.reference_answer: The sampled paths have a maximum length of 3 (N = 3); SQUIRE uses an encoder-decoder Transformer.

evidence.quote: with maximum lengthN = 3
encoder-decoder Transformer structure to translate the query to a path

questions.question: How many steps does SF-TQA's query generation have, and how much higher is its H@1 on TempQuestions than QUINT's?
questions.reference_answer: Two steps (constraint evocation and constraint grounding); its H@1 is 41.2 against 27.0 for QUINT, 14.2 points higher.

evidence.quote: The query generation consists of two steps

questions.question: How does CompAQT add alignment to the training loss, and how many questions does the paper use to structure its results discussion?
questions.reference_answer: It adds an alignment term to the loss that pulls the attention weights towards prior alignments built from heuristics (in the absence of gold alignments); the results are organised around four questions.

evidence.quote: we add the below term to the loss
we investigate the effectiveness of CompAQT through four questions

questions.question: On which five datasets does QADA report results, and what happens to the HotpotQA exact match when contrastive adaptation is removed?
questions.reference_answer: HotpotQA, NaturalQ., NewsQA, SearchQA and TriviaQA; without contrastive adaptation the HotpotQA EM drops from 50.80 to 48.21.

evidence.quote: Model HotpotQA NaturalQ. NewsQA SearchQA TriviaQA
w/o contrastive adaptation 48.21/64.54
a novel selfsupervised framework called QADA for QA domain adaptation

questions.question: By how much does the single-model open-domain QA approach beat the previous best, and on which two datasets is it evaluated?
questions.reference_answer: It outperforms the previous state of the art by 1.0 and 0.7 exact match points; it is evaluated on Natural Questions and TriviaQA.

evidence.quote: our model outperforms the previous state-of-the-art model by 1.0 and 0.7 exact match scores
Natural Questions (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019) and TriviaQA (Joshi et al., 2017)

questions.question: What do the authors of the long-form QA evaluation study conclude about automatic metrics, and how do they study what makes one answer better than another?
questions.reference_answer: No existing metric is predictive of human preference judgments; they analyse the free-form justifications collected from expert annotators (and WebGPT crowd annotators).

evidence.quote: no existing metrics are predictive of human preference judgments
we perform an analysis on the free-form justifications

questions.question: Which dataset is FAME evaluated on, how many entailment trees does it contain, and what structure does FAME build for its reasoning?
questions.reference_answer: EntailmentBank, with 1,840 expert-annotated entailment trees (converted to EntailmentBankQA); FAME organises its reasoning steps as a structured entailment tree.

evidence.quote: 1,840 expert-annotated entailment trees
The reasoning steps are organized as a structured entailment tree

questions.question: Which multi-hop architectures does the counterfactual multi-hop method get applied to besides BERT, and what problem does it set out to reduce?
questions.reference_answer: DFGN, HGN and XLNet in Dire; it targets the disconnected reasoning problem.

evidence.quote: DFGN (Qiu et al., 2019), HGN (Fang et al., 2019)
reduce the disconnected reasoning

questions.question: Which architecture is the WikiHowQA baseline built on, and how often did the first human-evaluation set-up prefer model answers over reference answers?
questions.reference_answer: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG); in the conventional human evaluation simpler model-generated answers were preferred over reference answers 48% of the time.

evidence.quote: we use the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
simpler modelgenerated answers were frequently (48% of the time) preferred over reference answers

questions.question: How many open-domain QA models and how many NQ-Open questions are used in the study of evaluation of open-domain QA with LLMs?
questions.reference_answer: 12 open-domain QA models; 301 questions randomly sampled from NQ-Open (1,490 unique question/answer pairs).

evidence.quote: assess 12 open-domain QA models
We randomly sample 301 questions from NQ

questions.question: How is the 'w/o head' training set of the long-tailed QA paper built, and between which kinds of tasks does the OLTQA model share knowledge?
questions.reference_answer: It is built by discarding the samples of head tasks, leaving samples from 16 tail tasks; the model shares knowledge between head, tail and unseen tasks.

evidence.quote: discarding samples from head tasks
knowledge sharing between head, tail and unseen tasks

questions.question: How many parameters does the ReasoningLM comparison list for EmbedKGQA, and what mismatch between components does ReasoningLM set out to remove?
questions.reference_answer: 125M parameters for EmbedKGQA; the divergence in model architecture between the pre-trained language model and the GNN module, which limits knowledge sharing.

evidence.quote: EmbedKGQA (Saxena et al., 2020) 125M
due to the divergence in model architecture, the PLM and GNN are not closely integrated

questions.question: What does GEMFormer put into its memory, and how much did its best memory improve joint F1 on HotpotQA?
questions.reference_answer: It first collects relevant information over the entire document into a global memory (tokens with entropy below a threshold); the best memory improved joint F1 by 1.6 points over the highest-performing memory-free baseline on HotpotQA.

evidence.quote: first collects relevant information over the entire document to the memory
by 1.6 joint F1 points for HP

questions.question: How does Hop, Union, Generate score a set of documents, and how does it learn rationales?
questions.reference_answer: A document-set scoring function (an MLP over the document embeddings and the question); it trains with a principled probabilistic approach and needs no rationale supervision.

evidence.quote: The document set scoring function is given by
a principled, probabilistic approach for training explainable multi

questions.question: Which score is the main metric for decontextualization in the LLM experiments, and into which stages does the proposed framework split the task?
questions.reference_answer: SARI-add (the F1 of added unigram edits, with BERTScore reported too); the framework has three stages: question generation, question answering and rewriting.

evidence.quote: we report SARI-add as our performance metric
decomposes the task into three stages: question generation, question answering, and rewriting

questions.question: What kind of method is the deep inductive logic reasoning paper, and why does it replace the minimum t-norm?
questions.reference_answer: A deep-learning based inductive logic reasoning method; the minimum t-norm is prone to a learning plateau because the gradient flows through only one input, so it proposes a neural logic operator.

evidence.quote: deep-learning based inductive logic reasoning method
minimum t-norm is prone to learning plateau

questions.question: How many training examples does the bandit-learning study start its systems from, and how is learning from feedback cast?
questions.reference_answer: Initial models are trained on 64, 256 or 1,024 examples; learning from feedback is cast as contextual bandit learning with simulated feedback.

evidence.quote: We obtain the sets of 64, 256, or 1,024
We cast the problem as contextual bandit learning

questions.question: Which of the two approaches, the unified knowledge interface or KGT5, uses a pretrained T5-Large, and which one trains a T5-small-sized model without pretrained weights?
questions.reference_answer: The unified knowledge interface (data-to-text generator) fine-tunes the pretrained T5-Large; KGT5 uses a model with the T5-small architecture trained without the pretrained weights.

evidence.quote: we use the pretrained T5-Large (Raffel et al., 2020) model as our generator
a model with the same architecture as T5-small

questions.question: Which two datasets do both KG-FiD and the single-model open-domain QA approach (YONO) use for their experiments, and which of them builds on FiD?
questions.reference_answer: Natural Questions and TriviaQA; KG-FiD builds on and improves FiD.

evidence.quote: Experiments on Natural Questions and TriviaQA
Natural Questions (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019) and TriviaQA (Joshi et al., 2017)

questions.question: How do the long-form QA evaluation study and the open-domain QA evaluation study differ in who judges the answers?
questions.reference_answer: The long-form study hires domain experts in seven areas to give preference judgments over pairs of answers; the open-domain study evaluates the answers of 12 models on 301 sampled questions with manual evaluation.

evidence.quote: We hire domain experts in seven areas to provide preference judgments over pairs of answers
assess 12 open-domain QA models

questions.question: Which core model does SQUIRE use to turn a query into a path, and which knowledge-graph QA paper deals with questions that have temporal intent?
questions.reference_answer: SQUIRE uses an encoder-decoder Transformer; SF-TQA (the semantic-framework approach) handles temporal questions over knowledge graphs.

evidence.quote: encoder-decoder Transformer structure to translate the query to a path
Answering factual questions with temporal intent over knowledge graphs

questions.question: Which two papers use counterfactuals, and for what does each use them?
questions.reference_answer: The retrieve-generate-filter paper creates counterfactual training and evaluation data; the counterfactual multi-hop QA paper uses counterfactual inference to disentangle disconnected reasoning.

evidence.quote: create counterfactual evaluation and training data with minimal human supervision
a counterfactual inference is proposed to disentangle the disconnected reasoning

questions.question: Which paper simulates user feedback to cut annotation and which one studies how users react to QA answers?
questions.reference_answer: The bandit-learning paper simulates feedback from supervised data to reduce data annotation; the background-information paper studies how users interact with QA systems and over-rely on predictions.

evidence.quote: analyze the characteristics of several learning scenarios with focus on reducing data annotation
we study how users interact with QA systems

questions.question: How do KG-FiD and ReasoningLM each bring knowledge-graph structure into a text model?
questions.reference_answer: KG-FiD uses a knowledge graph to establish structural relationships among the retrieved passages; ReasoningLM makes a pre-trained language model directly support subgraph reasoning for KGQA.

evidence.quote: uses a knowledge graph to establish the structural relationship among the retrieved passages
develop a more capable PLM that can directly support subgraph reasoning for KGQA

questions.question: Which paper splits its task into three stages and which splits query generation into two steps?
questions.reference_answer: The decontextualization framework (question generation, question answering, rewriting); SF-TQA (constraint evocation and constraint grounding).

evidence.quote: decomposes the task into three stages: question generation, question answering, and rewriting
The query generation consists of two steps

questions.question: Which approach relies on a multilingual dense retriever, and which one folds the retriever into the transformer itself?
questions.reference_answer: The cross-lingual attribution study models attributed QA with CORA, whose multilingual dense retriever MDPR is based on mBERT; the single-model open-domain QA approach casts the retriever and the reranker as internal passage-wise attention mechanisms inside the transformer.

evidence.quote: multilingual dense retriever ( MDPR ) which is based on mBERT
casting the retriever and the reranker as internal passage-wise attention mechanisms
